Answer: D
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) clearly shows the mass (white arrows) located in the posterior aspect of the thorax, behind the heart and trachea (star), which is characteristic of the posterior mediastinum. This location, combined with the displacement of adjacent structures like the aorta posteriorly, is most consistent with a neurogenic tumor, the most common primary posterior mediastinal mass.
